evidence: The compact filter retains the cold-disease gain: support≥5 gives 0.4681 / 0.5319 versus the full layer 0.4586 / 0.5388.
observation: Restricting disease phenotypes to HPO terms annotated to at least five graph diseases was tested on the same cold-disease split. It kept the borrowed-factor gain and even improved macro AUPRC slightly while cutting the annotation count, justifying the compact layer on cold-disease prediction as well as reachability.
subject: F-66
title: The support>=5 compact filter retains the cold-disease gain
